Question: For \(n\) a positive integer, let \(R(n)\) be the sum of the remainders when \(n\) is divided by \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) \(9,\) and \(10.\) For example, \[ \begin{aligned} &R(15) = 1 + 0 + 3 + 0 + 3 \\ &\quad {}+ 1 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 26. \end{aligned} \] How many two-digit positive integers \(n\) satisfy \[R(n) = R(n + 1)?\]
